Plans and status

Roadmap (Gantt chart)

Plans and status visuals show what happens when, who owns it and whether it is on track: the workplan pages of a steering-committee deck.

A roadmap puts a program's workstreams across fiscal quarters, with milestones and a today line. Status colors appear only in the status column and on missed milestones.

McKesson spec

  • Workstreams, not tasks; about ten rows at most
  • Flat, square bars: grey, blue for what the headline names
  • Status as a dot with its symbol, plus the word
  • Fiscal quarters and a dated today line
  1. 1Insight headlineCounts the exceptions and says why.
  2. 2SubtitleProgram, period, as-of date.
  3. 3Time headerPhases over fiscal years and quarters.
  4. 4One row per workstreamOwner as a role; related work together.
  5. 5StatusDot, symbol and word: never color alone.
  6. 6Flat barsGrey; blue only for the rows in the headline.
  7. 7MilestonesDiamonds: filled met, hollow due; a cross for missed.
  8. 8Today lineNavy, dashed, dated.
  9. 9The reason, drawnA navy arrow from the cause.
  10. 10Footnote and sourceDefine the statuses.

Plans and status

Initiative tracker

The status table behind the roadmap: one row per workstream, read in a minute at the start of a steering committee.

Lead with the roll-up and the exceptions. Everything below them is reference.

McKesson spec

  • Roll-up first: a count per status
  • Status column: dot, symbol and word
  • Off track, then at risk, then the rest
  • One accountable owner per row
  • "What changed" in one line, since the last report
  1. 1Insight headlineWhat needs a decision, and why.
  2. 2SubtitleWhat the columns hold; as-of date.
  3. 3Roll-upA count per status, exceptions first.
  4. 4Status columnA small dot with its symbol, and the word.
  5. 5Exceptions firstOff track, then at risk, in bold.
  6. 6OwnerOne accountable role per row.
  7. 7Next milestoneWith its date; a move says "was".
  8. 8What changedOne line since the last report.
  9. 9Footnote and sourceDefine each status.

Plans and status

Plans and status variants

The same rules throughout: status as a dot with symbol and word; data in grey and blue.

When a roadmap is the wrong chart

  • Progress to one target: a big number or a progress bar
  • Comparing units on a measure: bars, never status colors
  • Tasks, dates and hand-offs day to day: keep them in the project plan
  • How many people move through stages, and where they drop out: a Sankey

Milestone timeline

One workstream on one line, labels staggered. The Workday integration moved 3 months, so its original date stays visible.

Status over time

A symbol in every cell, today's word at the end. Skills inventory turned at risk in Jan; the two workstreams waiting on it went off track in Feb and Mar.

Status column in a scorecard

Data stays grey, orange only where it's worse: Skills inventory has used 71% of its budget in 50% of its time. Status gets its own column.

Process stages

Ordered stages take the blue-to-green steps, in order: sequence, not judgment. 34% of 1,200 academy nominees reached a data role.

Plans and status

Status best practice

Red, amber and green are loud. Give them one job, and never let them work alone.

Never color alone. Every dot carries its symbol (✓ ! ✕ –) and its word: red and green are the most common color-vision conflict.

Status, not data. Status colors mark workstreams and milestones. A measure gets grey and blue, and orange only when it's worse.

Flat and square. Small dots and thin rules; no pills, rounded boxes, shadows or gradients.

Exceptions first. Off track, then at risk; the rest in one grey line.

Never color alone

✕Try to avoidColored dots, nothing else.
✓RecommendedDot, symbol and word.

Status, not data

✕Try to avoidBars colored red to green by value.
✓RecommendedGrey, one blue, a target line.

Flat and square

✕Try to avoidPills, shadows, rounded headers.
✓RecommendedA small dot and hairlines.

Exceptions first

✕Try to avoidEvery row lit, in plan order.
✓RecommendedThe 3 exceptions, then a summary.

Plans and status

Roadmap best practice

A roadmap is read in seconds: where are we, what's late, and why.

One bar color. Grey bars, blue for the rows the headline names; names on the rows, not in a legend.

Workstreams, not tasks. Tasks belong in the project plan. The deck shows workstreams and their milestones.

Show today. A dated line makes "late" visible without reading a single date.

Show the slip. Keep the original date as a grey diamond and say "was Mar".

One bar color

✕Try to avoidA color per bar, decoded below.
✓RecommendedGrey, blue for the story; names on rows.

Workstreams, not tasks

✕Try to avoidThe project plan, pasted.
✓RecommendedWorkstreams and milestones.

Show today

✕Try to avoidNo sense of where we are.
✓RecommendedA labelled today line.

Show the slip

✕Try to avoidThe milestone quietly moved.
✓RecommendedOriginal date, arrow, "was Mar".

Plans and status

Build plans and status

No tool has one button for this, so the kit gives you the parts: mv.roadmap, mv.tracker and mv.status in Python, the roadmap and tracker slides in the starter deck, and the status pill and tracker table on the web.

docs/cookbook/plans-status.md · color.md: status colors

Before you send it

  • Status colors only on status: dots, missed milestones
  • Every dot has its symbol and its word
  • The roll-up matches the rows (2 off track, 1 at risk, 2 on track, 1 not started, 1 complete)
  • A dated today line; moved dates say "was"
  • One owner per row; the as-of date in the subtitle
PowerPoint

Starter deck slides 8 (roadmap) and 9 (tracker) are ready to copy. By hand: Tracker: Insert › Table; in the status column a small circle (Insert › Shapes › Oval, hold Shift) filled on track #00AF68, at risk #FFB500, off track #DA2103, not started #BFBFBF or complete #005A8C, with the symbol and word beside it. Gantt: a Stacked Bar of start and duration; start series Fill › No fill; Categories in reverse order; milestones and today line as shapes.

Excel

The same stacked-bar Gantt. In a tracker sheet, keep the status word in its own column and color a ● beside it with Conditional Formatting › New Rule › Use a formula to determine which cells to format (=$C2="Off track", font #DA2103). Skip icon sets: their red, yellow and green are Excel's, can't be changed, and carry no word.

Power BI

Table visual: a measure returning the status hex (SWITCH on the status), applied to a ● column with Cell elements › Font color › fx › Format style: Field value; the word in the next column. No native Gantt: use Deneb (Vega-Lite, with the kit's vega-lite-config.json) or an AppSource Gantt with the status colors set by hand.

Python

mv.roadmap, mv.tracker, mv.status_column and mv.status draw what these pages show: bars, ◆ ◇ ✕ milestones, slip arrows, a dated Today line, every status as colour, symbol and word. Plotly: px.timeline with mv.STATUS.

plan, ms = pd.read_csv("initiative_plan.csv"), pd.read_csv("initiative_milestones.csv")
mv.roadmap(ax, plan, ms, start="2025-04", end="2027-03", today="2026-03")
mv.tracker(ax2, plan, milestones=ms)   # exceptions first; status = dot, symbol, word
HTML

<span class="mck-status mck-status--off-track"> renders the dot, symbol and word from the tokens (also --on-track, --at-risk, --not-started, --done); .mck-tracker styles the table with exceptions in bold. Gantt: Plotly horizontal bars with base set to the start and mck.plotlyLayout("roadmap") from mck-viz.js.

R

geom_linerange() or geom_segment() for bars, geom_point(shape = 23) for milestone diamonds; status colors from mck_status, stage colors from mck_steps.
